audits.mathematicalReason: A regular hexagon has interior angles of 120°. At each contact vertex, the square turns clockwise through 360° − 120° − 90° = 150° before its next side contacts the next hexagon side. From diagram 1 to diagram 4 there are three such turns, totaling 450° clockwise, equivalent in orientation to 90° clockwise. The initially upward-pointing triangle therefore points right. Rotation properties, supported by polygon-angle and angle-arithmetic knowledge, adequately cover this route.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the rectangle have width w and height h. Triangle A has base h/n and perpendicular height w/2, so its area is wh/(4n). Triangle B has base w/m and perpendicular height h/2, so its area is wh/(4m). For positive subdivision counts n and m, their area ratio is [wh/(4n)]/[wh/(4m)] = m/n. Triangle area is the central assessed procedure, and rational-expression division supports this symbolic calculation.
